Mr. Abdus Salam Mamun, J: These Six Rules have been issued calling upon the Opposite Party to show cause as to why the impugned Judgment dated 31.12.1965 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court and Special Judge, Comilla dismissing the Special Appeal Nos. 30, 31, 33, 34, 35 and 36 of 1964 under Section 51 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act affirming the order of summary dismissals dated 18.1.1963 passed in Case Nos.12, 13, 14, 16, 17 and 56 of 1962 should not be set aside. 

 2. The petitioners Rai Saheb Abinash Chandra Bhattachaija and others preferred Six applications, being the Civil Revision Nos. 290 of I966. 291 of 1966, 292 of 1966, 993 of 1966, 294 of 1966 and 295 of 1966 before this Court under Section 115(1) or the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained 6(six) Rules thereupon impugning a judgment dated 31.12.1965 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court and Special Judge, Comilla in Special Appeal Nos. 30, 31, 33, 34, 35 and 36 of 1964 dismissing the Appeals on contest by the single Judgment that were filed under Section 51 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act,1950 stating in Civil Revision No.290 of 1966 that the land in question is a 13hiti. measuring, 24 feet X 18 feet, recorded in C.S. Plot No.1674 under the C.S. Khatian No.395 and the Petitioner took settlement of it under a registered Patta dated 30.11.1940 from the Ex.Landlord who was a Shebait of a Dehottar Estate, namely, The Sri Sri Gour Nityananda Mohapravu and Sri Sri Radha Govinda l3igraha with powers to make pucca and other constructions. 

 2(a). In the recent survey operation, the land has been recorded in the name of the Petitioner in plot No.3I28, under the Khatian No.527, in Mouza Brahmanbaria. Subsequently, a proceeding was started, being No.2734 of 1961 under Section 49 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for revision at the instance of the local Tahsildar on the grounds that the disputed land is a part of Taha-Bazar and khas land of the Ex-rent receiver: The petitioner contested the proceeding by submitting his written objections and stating, amongst other that the land in question was not the. Khas land of the Ex. land receiver. The Assistant Settlement Officer has allowed the objections of the Petitioner by his order dated 21.10.1961. But the Opposite Party preferred a Revisional application on the grounds that the disputed plot was within the ambit and periphery of the Ananda Bazar, whereupon the settlement officer directed a local enquiry by the Charge officer. Comilla and the charge officer submitted a report stating that the bulk area of Gagat Bazar would not be taken to be within the periphery of Fiat except two small plots. Viz 3725 and 3543, which might he kept under acquisition and the rest may by recorded in the names of the possessors:. The plot numbers 3170, 3167, 3157, 3156, 3145, 3144, 3232, 3134, 3139, 3136 and 3130 might be taken within the periphery of flat and recorded in the name of the Collector and the remaining plots might he recorded in the names of the .possessors and the Compensation Assessment Roll he corrected accordingly. 

 But on 18.8.1962 a notice was served upon the petitioner informing him that  compensation for the disputed land would be ascertained under Section 39 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as the same had been acquired by the Government under Section 3 of the said Act in the Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 1962. The Petitioner Tiled an objection against the notice to the Revenue Officer, but it was rejected summarily on 18.1.1963 without assigning any reason. The Petitioner thereafter, preferred the Special Appeal No.33 of 1964 in the Court of the learned Special Judge. Comilla against the said order, under Section 51 of the Act, but unfortunately, the same was also dismissed by order dated 31.12.1965. 

 2(c). In Civil Revision No. 292 of 1966 the Petitioner Mathur Chandra Pal and another were non-agricultural tenant in a bhiti, measuring 19 1/2 X 13 cubic feet recorded in Plot No. 3121 under the P.R.R. Khatian No. 524 by taking its settlement from the Ex. landlord who was a Sebait of the Debottor Estate by Registered Patta dated 18.3.1940 at yearly rental and dwelling therein by making pucca constructions of a two storied building and during the S.A: operation, the said bhiti was recorded in the names of the Petitioners as tenants under P.R.R. Khatian No. 524. Upon an objection filed by the opposite party, under Section 49 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, a case being No.2731 of 1961 was started and the Assistant Settlement Officer by his order dated 21.10.1961 upheld the records. But the Settlement Officer served a notice upon the Petitioners under Section 49 and 50 of the Act on 18.8.1962 in a Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1962 where the record was cancelled upon summary rejection of the Petitioner's objection and the learned Special Judge has also been pleased to dismiss the Special Appeal No. 70 of 1963 preferred by the Petitioners by his common judgment dated 31.12.1965. 

 others stated that they were non-agricultural tenants in a Bhiti, measuring 15 X 13 cubic feet in Part of C.S. Plot No. 1674 under the C.S. Khatian No. 369/395 under a registered Patta dated 25.5.1942 executed by the Ex-landlord i.e, the Sebait of the Debottar Estate at yearly rental and was living therein by making pucca constructions and it was recorded in the names of the Petitioners in Plot No. 3125 under the P.R.R. Khatian No.526 and at the instance of the Tahsilder. a Miscellaneous Case No.2733 of 1961 was started on the grounds that the bhiti was part of the Ananda Bazar and the Assistant Settlement Officer dismissed the said Miscellaneous Case by his Order dated 21.10.1961. But the Settlement Officer served upon them a notice on 18.12.1962 in the Miscellaneous Case No.I4 of 1962, in which their objections were dismissed summarily on 14.1.1963 and the learned' special Judge has also been pleased to dismiss the Special Appeal no.73 of 1963, renumbered as the Special Appeal No. 35 of 1964, by a common judgment dated 31.12.1965. 

 2(e). In Civil Revision No.294 of 1966 the Petitioner Rebati Mohan Chowdhury stated  that he is a non-agricultural tenant in a Bhiti, measuring 23 X 20 cubic feet recorded in C.S. Plot No. 1674 under the C.S. Khatian No. 369/395 under a Patta from the Ex-landlord who was a Sebait of the Debottar Estate about 25 years age and was living by raising big structures and the P.R.R. Khatian No523 was prepared in his name which was unheld by the Assistant Settlement Officer in Miscellaneous Case No.2730 dated 13.11. 1961. But the record was cancel led by the Settlement Officer in Miscellaneous case No. 56 of 1962 on 15.1.1963 and the learned Special Judge also has been pleased to dismiss the Special Appeal No. 25 of 1963, renumbered as the Special Appeal No. 36 of 1964 preferred by this Petitioner' in a common judgment dated 31.12.1965. 

 2(f). In Civil Revision No.295 of 1966; the Petitioner Madhabilata Baisnabi stated that  she is a non-agricultural tenant in a bhiti, measuring 15 X 13 cubic feet in Part of C.S Plot No. 1674 under the C.S. Khatian No. 369/395, under a registered Patta dated 29.11.1940, executed by the Ex-landlord. who is the Sebaits of the Debottar Property at the yearly rental, having her two-storied structures therein with pucca wall and it was recorded in the P.R.R. Plot No. 3122 under the P.R.R. Khatian No. 525 in her name and the Assistant Settlement Officer upheld the recording. but the Settlement Officer cancelled it in the Miscellaneous Case No.16 'of 1962, by an order dated 14.1.1963 and her Special Appeal No. 72 of 1963, renumbered as the Special Appeal No. 34 of 1964, was also dismissed by the Special Judge in a common judgment dated 31.12.1965. 

 3. The grounds of the petitioners for preferring these applications are common and they are : the Learned Special Judge has acted illegally and without jurisdiction in passing the impugned judgment and order and the Learned Special Judge has acted illegally in holding that the disputed plots are situated within the Ananda Bazar overlooking the report of the Charge Officer, dated 18.7.1962 and has erred also in law in not holding that the Petitioners are non-agricultural tenants in a Debottar Estate which cannot be acquired and also in upholding the assessments made by the revenue officials at smaller amounts for the properties, worth of several times more. 

 By office note dated 11.4.2004, it was stated that the Petitioner No. 1, 2(a)-2(h) and 3 have died and the N-I 0 notice has returned unnerved and that no step has been taken for 

 Opposite Party on 03.4.1967 through the Sub-Divisional Manager, Government Acquired Estate, Sadar North. Comilla in all the Rules and the Affidavit-in-Reply filed on behalf of the Petitioners on 7.5.1967 in reply thereto who found no entry in the Order Book. 

 7. By the aforesaid Counter-Affidavit, the Opposite Party has stated that the C.S. Plot 

 Plot No.1674 was recorded in the names of the persons who were ex-rent receivers and the rent-receiving interests have been acquired by the Province Of East Pakistan by the Notification dated 2nd April. 1956 and the property has vested in the province of East Pakistan free from encumbrances under Section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (2nd Amendment) Ordinance, 1960 (East Pakistan Ordinance No. XII of 1960). 

 In the C.S. Nos.395 and 369 one Radhika Mohan Chowdhury and others were the ex. Rent-receivers under Touzi No.203 in the Pargana "Shatrakhandai" of the Comilla Collectorate. There is no record in the office to show whether these ex. Rent-receivers were Sebait of any Debottar Estate. 

 According to the provisions of the Ordinance No. IX of 1960 the Sahait of a Debottar Estate was to act as an agent under the Provincial Government for management ()I' such estate and was liable to submit statements and accounts to the collector of the District. But no such Sebait as alleged in respect of properties in question ever approached the authority for appointment as agent of Debottar property and it is not known whether the properties in question were at any time Debottar properties. 

 The kind in question falls within a Bazar area and have rightly been acquired and compensation assessed on acquisition. Under the provisions of Act X of 1953 the unauthorized occupants are liable to eviction from Government acquired Hat and Bazar. 

 8. In the Affidavit-in-reply, the Petitioners stated that it was not a fact that the C.S. Plot  No.1674 was acquired by the Opposite Party on 2.4.1956 as non-retainable khan land of the Ex-rent receivers and that Radhika Mohan Chowdhury was a Sebait of Sree Sree Nittayananda Mohaprovu and Sree Sree Radha Govinda Bigraha. The suit land is not covered by the Bazar and the Petitioners are not unauthorized occupants and that the Miscellaneous Cases were dismissed summarily'. 

 9. In the impugned order dated 31.8.1965, passed in Special Appeal Nos. 30. 31. 33, 34. 35 and 36 of 1964 preferred against the order of the Settlement Officer, in-charge. Comilla made in Miscellaneous Case Nos. 12 of 1962, 17 or 1962, 13 of 1962, 16 of 1961, 14 of 1962 and 56 of 1962 the Learned Sub-ordinate Judge and Special Judge, Comilla held that in view of the amendment made in Section 20 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act through promulgation of the East Pakistan Ordinance No. XII of 1960 filing of fresh Petitioners under section 49 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act by the Tahsildar of the Government Acquired Estate cannot he said illegal. 

 The disputed lands are situated in a Bazar which is proved by some of the Dakhilas filed by the appellants themselves. Whether the disputed lands are Debottar lands or not should he decided by a competent Court. As the disputed lands are situated in a Bazar which is known as Ananda Bazar, the Settlement Officer is not wrong in allowing the assessment of compensation directing correction of records under Section 49 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 'Hat or Bazar' has been defined under Section 2(12) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950 providing that "...Hat' or 'Bazar' means any place Where persons assemble daily or on particular days in a week primary for the purposes of buying or selling agricultural produce, livestock, paultry, hides, skins, meat, fish, eggs, milk, milk-products or any other articles of food or drink or other necessaries of life, and includes all shops of such articles or manufactured articles within such place." 

 While the Section 3 of the Act provided general provisions for acquisition of all rent- receiving interests by the Provincial Government wiping out the rent-receiving intermediary interests completely the Section 20 made an exception to the general provision providing a list of land which the rent-receivers cultivating raiyats cultivating under raiyats and non-agricultural tenants may retain in their possession as khan land. Sub-section 2(a) of Section 20 is again an exception to the exception provided by Section 20. This Sub-Section 2(a) to Section 20 provides that "Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any instrument or in any judgment or decree or order of any Court lands of the classes referred to in the clauses (a) and (h) of sub-section (2) do not include and shall be deemed never to have included — 

 This sub-section (2a) was substituted for the 'Explanation' of the original Section by the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1960 (East Pakistan Ordinance No. XII of 1960). Prior to the substitution, there was the. 'Explanation' under this Section, explaining that "for the purpose or clause (a) lands covered by building do not include Hats or Bazars." 

 As such, sub-section 2(a) to the Section 20, by way of substitution, has introduced an elementary change in the notion and definition of the terms 'Flat' or 'Bazar' their periphery and dimensions. This sub-section 2(a) was introduced following the judgment delivered in the case of Yusuf Ali Chowdhury Vs. the Province of East Pakistan reported in 11 DLR (SC) 316 setting aside the decision of the High Court reported in 9 DLR 674 and made with the view to nullify the effect of the ruling of the Supreme court and thus the implication of this ordinance is that the Flats and Bazars are subject to acquisition by the Government irrespective of lands covered by building. 

 11. On perusal of the grounds taken in these applications, it appears that the grievances of the Petitioners arc two 'bids: namely, the land in question belonged to a Debottar Estate and the Debottar Property cannot be acquired by the Provincial Government. The Petitioners Rai Shaheb and others were non-agricultural tenants in the Debottar property by taking settlement from its Sebait, and secondly the land in question did not belong to a Bazar namely the Ananda Bazar and cannot he acquired as such. 

 In the case of Jihendra Kishore Roy Chowdhury Vs. the Province of East Pakistan. reported in 9 DI.R(SC) 21, it was held that a Mutwalli or a Sebait is a rent-receiver within the meaning of clause (23) of section 2 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950. 

 This case arose out of the Notification No.4839- L.R. issued on 2nd April, 1956 under  sub-section (1) to Section 3 of the Act acquiring of the interests of certain rent-receivers, which was decided by a Full Bench or the then High Court at Dhaka including his Lordship. the Chief Justice Amin Ahmed and reported in 8 DER 457 (The Chief' Justice took pride of its authorship and presented a copy of the printed judgment to Mr. Justice Douglas. while his Lordship was visiting the United States. see "A peep into the past," by Former Chief Justice Amin Ahmed. Page-61). It was held in this case that the Notification was applicable to a Mutwalli or Sebait, thereby divesting them from their interests in the land which whether they vested in the Almighty or a Deity or for the purpose of the Act in the Mutwalli or the Sebait are from the date of the Notification transferred absolutely to the Provincial Government and as per the decision given in the case of Khondakar Ali Afzal Vs. the Province of East Pakistan reported in 18 DLR184, the outgoing Mutwalli or Sebait becomes entitled to compensation as provided in the Act. 

 12. In the Counter Affidavits the Opposite Party stated that one Radhika Mohan Chowdhury and others were the ex. Rent-receivers of touzi No.203 under the Pargana 'Shatrakhandi' in the C.S. Plot No. 1674 under the C.S. Khatian No.395/369 and there is no record in the office of the Collactorate. Comilla to show whether these ex. Rent-receivers were Sebait or that the property was Debottar. Under the provisions of the Ordinance No. IX of 1960, the Sebait of the Debottar Property were to act as agent under the Provincial Government for management of such an estate and were liable to submit statements and accounts to the Collector or the District but no such Sebait as alleged in respect ()I' the properties involved ever approached the authority for appointment of agent. 

 In the Affidavit-in-Reply the Petitioners stated that the failure of Sehaits to submit any statement or accounts to the Collector cannot extinguish the right of the Deities and that of the Petitioners as tenants under the Deities. 

 If for argument's sake the contentions of the Petitioners are accepted that the property in question is Debottor Property and Radhika Mohan Chowdhury and others were Sehaits of Deities and the Petitioners were non-agricultural tenants under their pattas even then, the property was not immune from acquisition in view of the case of Jibendra Kishore Roy Chowdhury supra. 

 15. The Petitioners next contended that the land in question is not situated within the periphery or a Bazar. In support of their contentions the Petitioners stated that a local enquiry was held on 18.7.1962 by one Mr. S. Ahmed. Charge Officer. Comilla who held that Ananda Bazar was more or less compact block intervened here and there by shops lying in the following  plots which might be taken to he within the periphery of Hat and recorded in the name of the Collector, viz. Plots No. 3170. 3167. 3157. 3156. 3144. 3132. 313-1. 3139. 3136 and 3130 and the Plots of the Petitioners were not included and they have been recorded in the names of the Petitioners. 

 In the Counter Affidavits, the Opposite Party has stated that the C.S. Plot No. 1674 has been classed as a Hat known as Ananda Bazar and during the S.A. operation, the C.S Plot No. 1674 has been split up in S.A. Plot Nos. 3119. 3120. 3121. 3122. 3123. 3124. 3125. 3126. 3127, 3128 and 3130 covered by Ananda Bazar within the Brahmanbaria Municipal Area. If the C.S. Plot No. 1674 has been split up in those S.A. plots and the C.S. Plot itself' was classed as Hat, namely. Ananda Bazar, it is really an exception that all the above plots have been acquired as Bazar except the Plots of the Petitioners which situate in between. The Petitioner Rai Shaheb himself stated that he is carrying on business in one part of the building and sub-let the other part to monthly tenants also for carrying on business. In the Affidavit-in-reply, the Petitioners stated nothing about this split up of the C.S. Plot No.1674 and acquisition or all other surroundings plots. If the C.S. Plot No. 1674 was recorded as a Hat. there is no reason why the splitting plots shall not be classed as Hat. 

 16. Admittedly, the S.A. record-of-rights have not been prepared in the names of the Petitioners. In paragraph 7 of the Counter-Affidavits, submitted in the C.R. No. 290 of 1966 the Opposite Party, Government stated that "it is not a fact that the P.R.R. Khatian No. 4527 with Plot No. 3129 was opened in his name. One Khatian No.527 was opened in his name with Plot No. 3128 which has been subsequently cancelled by the Settlement Officer. Comilla by a proceeding under Section 49 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 1962 by S.D.O. Comilla on 18.1.1963." 

 17. About the Local enquiry and Report thereof: this Opposite Party stated that "the deponent is not aware of any such enquiry by such charge officer. The Settlement Officer also did not take into -account of such an enquiry report and passed order in favour of the Province of East Pakistan and prepared the C.A. Roll accordingly and opened R.O.R. in favour of the Province." 

 The Petitioners themselves stated in their applications that "they applied for certified copy of the said order which was not supplied to them by the Revenue Officer, but the same will be seen it' the records are called for." 

 19. Section 49 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (substituted by East Bengal Act No. V of 1956) reads as follows: 

 21. Mr. Harendra Nath Nandi, the learned Advocate, appearing for the Petitioners submits that in the instant Rules. Section 20(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 shall be applicable and the interest of a non-agricultural tenant is protected from acquisition tinder this Section. 

 The impugned Judgment and Order dated 31.12.1965 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Juke. 3rd Court, Comilla and the Special Judge dismissing the Special Appeal Nos. 30. 31. 33. 34. 35 and 36 of 1964 under Section 51 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and affirming the order of summary dismissals dated 18.1.1963 passed in Miscellaneous Case Nos. 12. 13. 14. 16. 17 and 56 of 1962 is hereby upheld. Send down the Lower Court's Records at once.
